items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: So when they ended the first set, the trombone, Wes Cope was his name, he came over and he said, “the old man wants to know if you want to join the band.”

ctx.x: No I don’t think they called it quits — I think the big band era started to go in actually about ’48. When I got out of the Army I mean and I had the chance to audition for Les Paul, who at the time had a jazz trio. And I went up and luckily, thanks to my teacher and the technique he taught me you know, I could keep up with Les. And his idea of a ballad was about here [claps]. So I played with the group. We started at a place called the Rounders Club, which was literally at the corner of Sunset and Vine at the…

whether my reading ability, that would be like the first studio work, working on a radio show. That’s what I wanted to do eventually. And we had about a three week break there before we started the show and I went back to San Diego and I got a call from a guy who had been the trombonist way early with Ozzie Nelson, who he was playing trombone for Tommy Dorsey’s band, and he was kind of a road manager. And he called me up and he said, “we’re coming into town next Friday” and he said, “would you like to play one…
In addition to playing with Dorsey, you’ve got to play the other people’s music.
